If the athlete resides in a different county, then two years' continuous residence must be established if he wishes to "adopt" the county in which he lives. Hugh Barrow (Scotland)

HUGH BARROW sends his regards to all, particularly that "nut-case" fellow scotsman, Bill Kerr. Hugh has been troubled with a persistent leg injury this winter which caused him to miss the Scottish National and a BAAAB trip to LYON for a 2,000 metres indoor race.

Hugh Barrow completes his 14 months qualification period in March and thereafter will be first claim Belgrave. At one time Hugh had anticipated moving to London permanantly but finally decided to remain in Glasgow and travel as often as possible - hence his 14 months wait.
FRONT COVER (Photo:R.Linstead) A fine study of Hugh Barrow, who had two memorable runs for Belgrave last month. Our picture was taken in our road relay (see P.14).

Hugh Barrow will certainly not forget his first road relay in Belgrave colours. Taking the 11th stage the 21 year old Scotsman set off 7 seconds behind John Cooke of Portsmouth and with a great spell of running turned this deficit into a 2 second lead - despite a fast finish from international Cooke.

On the first leg of the return journey Adcocks ran for Coventry, Bruce Tulloh for Portsmouth and we had Hugh Barrow. Tulloh was in great form and took his team into the lead with a record breaking run which lowered the stage record by fifteen seconds.
North, O'Hara, Dabbs, Thorpe and Black were to be joined by Hugh Barrow for the "National" at Sheffield, leaving runners of the class of Steer, Reilly and Hart as reserves.
Belgrave's depth was illustrated by the fact that Geoff North and Hugh Barrow were on the sidelines and all six of Belgrave's short stage runners were amongst the day's fastest dozen for that course.
Albert is a friend of Bill Kerr and Hugh Barrow. He ran for us in the Banks match at Epsom, splitting Bicourt and Dance, and displayed a keenness that we were sorry to lose so soon.
In the Scottish Maryhill "Nigel Barge" 4½ miles road race on January 7th, Hugh Barrow finished 11th in 22:52. First two home were Ian McCafferty (M'well) 21:58 and Lachie Stewart (V/Leven). 22:15.
